_metadata.independence: I read only x13-rc-input.json and no other file, repository content, web page or API.

hints.reason: WHITE completes Snow White (SNOW), and Snow White's best-known story beat is the poisoned apple (APPLE); a clean one-step fairy-tale route.

pairs.pair_note: Solid fairy-tale clue; POISON would be an alternative but no stronger.

hints.reason: Queen the rock band (BAND) and a queen who wears a crown (CROWN); a clear, familiar double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Note QUEEN is also a target in p_band__queen; avoid both pairs on one board.

hints.reason: Brass band is a stock phrase (BAND) and horns are the classic brass instruments (HORN); fair and immediate.

pairs.pair_note: Straightforward, accurate.

hints.reason: MERCURY -> Freddie Mercury -> frontman of Queen (QUEEN), which is a band (BAND); indirect familiar knowledge with a real aha, past the planet and element decoys.

pairs.pair_note: Good RELATIVE-style indirect route; FREDDIE would be more direct but flatter.

hints.reason: Marching band nails BAND, but SCHOOL is only a setting where marching bands appear (parades, the military and colleges compete for it), while ROCK gives rock band plus the film School of Rock for both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Prefer ROCK (rock band / School of Rock); MARCHING is accurate but leans on BAND alone.

hints.reason: EARTH -> Earth, Wind & Fire, the famous band (BAND) whose name contains WIND; the band name is instantly familiar and the elements echo helps it click.

pairs.pair_note: Band-name phrase-join, but a well-known one; FIRE would work equally well.

hints.reason: Bath towel (BATH) and beach towel (BEACH) are both everyday compounds; easy and clean.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, satisfying phrase-join.

hints.reason: Sandcastles are built on the beach (BEACH) and a king lives in a castle (KING); both images are immediate.

pairs.pair_note: CASTLE is also the hint for p_chess__sand; keep them off the same board or batch run.

hints.reason: Bees live in a hive (BEE) and the beehive is a famous tall hairdo (HAIR, think Marge Simpson); a genuine aha.

pairs.pair_note: One of the nicer ones in the batch.

hints.reason: A bike chain (BIKE) and the rattling chains of ghosts like Marley's (GHOST); two unrelated images joined neatly.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasant surprise pairing.

hints.reason: You make a wish blowing out birthday candles (BIRTHDAY) and wish upon a shooting star (STAR); warm and instantly clear.

pairs.pair_note: Lovely, easy clue.

hints.reason: A boat's deck (BOAT) and a deck of cards (CARD); a classic double meaning.
hints.fix: A boat has a deck, and cards come in a deck.

pairs.pair_note: Explanation wording 'so do cards' is slightly loose (cards don't have a deck); suggested fix above.

hints.reason: Boxers fight in a ring (BOXER) and a phone rings (PHONE); a clean noun/verb double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and fair.

hints.reason: Cameras have a lens (CAMERA) and so does the human eye (EYE); accurate and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, accurate.

hints.reason: A car's hood (CAR, U.S. usage) and a coat's hood (COAT); a good double meaning for a U.S. audience.

pairs.pair_note: Works well in U.S. English (British would say bonnet).

hints.reason: Bridge the card game (CARD) and a bridge over a river (RIVER); a satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Cats have paws (CAT), and 'paws' is common slang for hands ('keep your paws off') or to paw at something with your hand (HAND); the explanation should state that slang rather than claim a paw is literally a hand.
hints.fix: A cat walks on paws, and 'paws' is slang for hands, as in 'Keep your paws off!'

pairs.pair_note: Fine idea; the current HAND line ('A paw is an animal's hand') is loose, since paws are feet; the fix uses the true slang route.

hints.reason: The rook is commonly called a castle and castling is a chess move (CHESS), and sand builds sandcastles (SAND); both routes are familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Duplicate hint word with p_beach__king; the CHESS line could say 'The rook is often called a castle' for precision, but it is not false.

hints.reason: GLASS -> the glass slipper, which Cinderella loses (CINDERELLA) and which is a shoe (SHOE); more interesting than SLIPPER, which would be a near-synonym of SHOE.

pairs.pair_note: Good; one-step fairy-tale route.

hints.reason: A computer virus (COMPUTER) and doctors treating viral illness (DOCTOR); the same pattern as COMPUTER + INSECT -> BUG.

pairs.pair_note: 'Doctors treat viruses' is acceptable shorthand for viral infections.

hints.reason: Donkey is Shrek's sidekick (DONKEY) and Dragon is the dragon who falls for him (DRAGON); a fun, very familiar film route.
hints.fix: Dragon falls for Donkey, and by the sequels she is his wife.

pairs.pair_note: Idea is strong; the DRAGON line 'Donkey marries the Dragon' implies an on-screen wedding I am not certain the films show, so a safer wording is offered.

hints.reason: You flush a toilet (TOILET) and a flushed face goes red (FACE); a clean double meaning that stays PG.

pairs.pair_note: Nice.

hints.reason: A fence post (FENCE) and post meaning mail, as in post office and postage (MAIL); a solid double meaning familiar in the U.S.

pairs.pair_note: 'Post a letter' leans slightly British; a MAIL line like 'The post office delivers mail.' would feel more American, but nothing is false.

hints.reason: A school of fish (FISH) and teachers working at a school (TEACHER); a classic double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Classic.

hints.reason: Flowers bloom (FLOWER) and spring is blooming season (SPRING); flat but honest and clear for both.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, low delight; acceptable.

hints.reason: A football fan (FOOTBALL) and an electric fan that cools you in summer (SUMMER); the SUMMER side is a use-association rather than a phrase, but the double meaning clicks.

pairs.pair_note: SUMMER side is softer than FOOTBALL; still fair.

hints.reason: A game ending in a tie (GAME) and a necktie worn with a dress shirt (SHIRT); tie-dye shirt is a bonus route.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Golf club the stick (GOLF) and nightclub the venue (NIGHT); two senses of CLUB, both instant.

pairs.pair_note: Same shape as BUS + GOLF -> DRIVER.

hints.reason: A lion's mane (LION) is its hair, and people speak of a full mane of hair (HAIR); synonym-of-one-sense, but it honestly links both.

pairs.pair_note: Easy; the synonym flag is a note only.

hints.reason: Jack Frost (JACK) is the familiar winter sprite, and frost and snow go together as winter weather (SNOW); the Jack Frost name makes it click.

pairs.pair_note: SNOW side is a property association rather than a phrase; fine for an easy clue.

hints.reason: King Kong the movie ape (KING) and Donkey Kong the classic arcade game (VIDEO GAME); both names are iconic and the pairing is fun.

pairs.pair_note: A phrase-join that earns its place.

hints.reason: A knight in armor (KNIGHT) and a turtle's shell as natural armor (TURTLE); an accepted metaphor, not a false fact.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: A key opens a lock (LOCK) and music is written in a key (MUSIC); a classic double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Classic.

hints.reason: Zorro is the masked hero (MASK, as in The Mask of Zorro) who fights with a sword (SWORD); both are his defining traits.

pairs.pair_note: Strong character clue.

hints.reason: The Pied Piper plays his pipe (MUSIC) to lead the rats out of town (RAT); a crisp fairy-tale route.

pairs.pair_note: Very good.

hints.reason: PIZZA -> the pizza-loving Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, which supplies both NINJA and TURTLE at once; indirect, familiar and fun.

pairs.pair_note: Nice indirect route; MUTANT would be more direct but flatter.

hints.reason: The third little pig's brick house (PIG) and brick walls (WALL); fairy tale plus everyday material.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Pirate ship (PIRATE) and spaceship (SPACE) are both instant compounds; easy but clean.

pairs.pair_note: Simple phrase-join; acceptable.

hints.reason: Princess Peach (PRINCESS) is the Mario series princess (VIDEO GAME); the fruit decoy makes the click pleasant.

pairs.pair_note: ZELDA would also work here, but it is used for p_sword__video-game.

hints.reason: Ursula is The Little Mermaid's sea witch, living under the sea (SEA) and a witch (WITCH); a direct, broadly known Disney route.

pairs.pair_note: Good Disney clue.

hints.reason: FIFA is soccer's world governing body (SOCCER) and the name of EA's long-running soccer game series (VIDEO GAME); strong, but EA renamed the series EA Sports FC in 2023, so the text should not present FIFA as the current game.
hints.fix: FIFA runs world soccer, and its name was on EA's hugely popular soccer video game series for three decades.

pairs.pair_note: Still widely recognized (and FIFA is in the news with the 2026 U.S. World Cup); just past-tense the video game claim.

hints.reason: The Legend of Zelda is an iconic video game series (VIDEO GAME), and its hero Link's Master Sword is its emblem (SWORD); the sword side takes one extra step since Zelda herself is not the swordsman.

pairs.pair_note: SWORD side is one step removed but the Master Sword is famous enough.
